The tumdak' is a two-headed hand-struck membranophone used by the Santal of eastern India and Bangladesh. The body is cylindrical, made of clay; the two heads are usually cowhide, the right slightly smaller than the left, and each has a round patch of tuning paste at the centre to strengthen the sound. When dancing, the player hangs the drum from the neck on a rope or strap and strikes it with the whole hand and fingers in time. It belongs with the dholak, nal and mridangam among the two-headed Indian hand drums, and is often used with the tamak' in religious ritual and festivals, and it is played almost entirely by men.
